featured_reviews.name: 光頭小伍
featured_reviews.review_text:
走進孟買的心臟，你會來到一個讓世界又震撼又敬佩的地方——Dharavi。這裡面積僅約1.75平方公里，卻容納了數十萬人口，是亞洲最密集的社區之一。但如果你只用「貧民窟」來定義它，那就太小看這裡了。

在狹窄巷弄之間，藏著驚人的經濟能量。回收、皮革、紡織、陶器，一間間小工坊日夜運轉，創造出數億美元的產值，產品甚至銷往世界各地。這裡沒有華麗辦公室，卻有最真實的創業精神；沒有資源優勢，卻用雙手打造無限可能。

來自印度各地的人們在此落腳，不同語言、宗教與文化交織，形成獨特的生命力。儘管面對擁擠與衛生挑戰，他們依然努力生活、努力工作，用韌性撐起整個城市的運轉。

達拉維不是悲情的象徵，而是一面鏡子，讓人看見人在困境中依然可以發光。走一趟，你會重新理解什麼叫做努力，什麼叫做希望。
featured_reviews.review_translated_text:
Step into the heart of Mumbai, and you'll find a place that both shocks and inspires awe—Dharavi. Spanning only about 1.75 square kilometers, it houses hundreds of thousands of people, making it one of the most densely populated communities in Asia. But to define it merely as a "slum" would be a gross underestimation.

Hidden within its narrow alleyways is an astonishing economic energy. Recycling, leather, textiles, pottery—small workshops operate day and night, generating hundreds of millions of dollars in revenue, with products sold worldwide. Here, there are no glamorous offices, but the most genuine entrepreneurial spirit; no resource advantages, but limitless possibilities created with their own hands.

People from all over India have settled here, their diverse languages, religions, and cultures intertwining to create a unique vitality. Despite facing overcrowding and sanitation challenges, they persevere, working hard and resiliently keeping the city running.

Dharavi is not a symbol of tragedy, but a mirror reflecting the light that shines even in adversity. A visit will give you a new understanding of the meaning of hard work and hope.

featured_reviews.name: Brett Hansen
featured_reviews.review_text:
We joined the ethical walking tour of Dharavi slums with Reality Tours & Travel and it was one of the most eye opening and meaningful experiences of our time in Mumbai, India.

Our guide Diksha was excellent. She is a young Gen Z woman who is incredibly wise, well informed and very articulate. She explained the social, economic and cultural realities of Dharavi with clarity and compassion, and was always happy to answer questions along the way.

What I appreciated most about this tour is that it focuses primarily on the businesses and industries operating within Dharavi rather than treating it like a spectacle. We saw small scale recycling operations, leather workshops, pottery areas and many other hardworking micro industries. It was fascinating to learn how much manufacturing and production takes place here. At times we also walked through incredibly narrow pathways between homes, sometimes only about a metre wide, which gave a sense of just how densely populated the area is.

Dharavi has an estimated population of between 700,000 and 1 million people living in only about 2.1 square kilometres, so the energy and activity is intense. People work extremely hard. Many workers come from other regions of India, sending money home to their families and only seeing them once or twice a year. Some sleep at their workplaces and work 12 to 15 hour days. It is a tough life and seeing this reality firsthand is humbling.

One of the most confronting things we learned is that materials produced in Dharavi are sometimes used by high end international brands. However, the origin is often labelled simply as “Made in India” rather than Dharavi because of the stigma attached to the area. That was heartbreaking to hear given the skill and effort of the people working there.

Photography and video are not allowed on the tour, which is completely fair and respectful. It keeps the focus on learning rather than treating people’s lives as a spectacle.

Another reason to support this tour is that 80 percent of the profits go back into local education programs run by the organisation. While schooling in India is compulsory, class sizes can be around one teacher to 50 students. Reality Tours supports supplementary learning including English and IT classes, along with scholarships for local students.

The tour was scheduled for about 90 minutes but ended up running for closer to two hours and fifteen minutes, so we were definitely tired by the end, but it was absolutely worth it.

If you want to better understand a part of Mumbai that many visitors never see, this slum tour is thoughtful, respectful and genuinely educational. It reminds you that there are whole worlds of experience beyond our own daily lives, and that they are worth learning about with empathy and respect.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Thank you for such a thoughtful and detailed review. We are really glad to hear that the tour was a meaningful and eye-opening part of your time in Dharavi.

It’s wonderful to know that Diksha made the experience engaging and informative, and that you appreciated the focus on the industries and hardworking communities that make Dharavi so unique. We are also grateful that you highlighted our no-photography policy and the importance of respectful tourism.

Thank you as well for mentioning the education programs supported by Reality Tours & Travel, your support helps make those initiatives possible. We truly appreciate you recommending the tour and hope the experience stays with you long after your visit to Mumbai. 🙏
